import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create an insightful visualization: Survival probability by Passenger Class and Sex
# Using seaborn.catplot with kind='bar' to show the mean survival rate
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='pclass',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    kind='bar',
    palette='viridis',  # Choose a color palette
    height=6,           # Height of the plot
    aspect=1.2,         # Aspect ratio
    errorbar='sd'       # Show standard deviation as error bars
)

# Set main title for the figure
g.fig.suptitle("Survival Probability on the Titanic by Passenger Class and Sex", y=1.02, fontsize=16)

# Set axis labels
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Probability")

# Customize x-axis tick labels for better readability
pclass_labels_map = {1: '1st Class', 2: '2nd Class', 3: '3rd Class'}
g.set_xticklabels([pclass_labels_map[int(tick.get_text())] for tick in g.ax.get_xticklabels()])

# Set legend title
g.legend.set_title("Sex")

# Add a grid for better readability on the y-axis
g.ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
